name: pause-mid-sentence
why: A 2.5 s freeze while looking for a word. Grok's word times must show the silence.
script: Last weekend I went to the [2.5 pause] farmers market with my sister

name: pause-natural-short
why: A 1 s thinking pause is normal and must not be flagged.
script: Last weekend I went to the [1.0 not pause] farmers market with my sister

name: pause-edge-1.3
why: A real 1.3 s pause should not be flagged. Grok word edges add about 0.2 s, so this sits right on the line.
script: Last weekend I went to the [1.3 not pause] farmers market with my sister

name: pause-just-over
why: 1.7 s is over the line. Grok rounding must not hide it.
script: My favourite place to eat is a small [1.7 pause] noodle shop near the station

name: pause-before-first-word
why: Freezing before saying anything is a pause too.
script: [2.5 pause] Well I think the best part of my job is the people

name: fillers-close
why: Two fillers a few seconds apart. Grok must keep them with filler_words on. (The Mac voice needs “umm,” / “uhh,” spellings to sound like fillers.)
script: The best part of my job is, <fillers> umm, the people I work with and, uhh, </> the long lunches

name: fillers-three
why: Three fillers in a row while stuck.
script: And then we, <fillers> umm, uhh, umm, </> took the train home

name: fillers-far-apart
why: Fillers spread out across normal speech are not a stuck moment.
script: <not fillers> Umm, so every morning I walk to the station and buy a coffee from the same small shop on the corner and then I read the news on the train until, uhh, </> I arrive at work

name: restart-one-word
why: “I, I went” restart. Grok must keep both copies.
script: Yesterday <restart> I I </> went to the cinema

name: restart-phrase
why: “I went to, I went to the market” restart.
script: On Sunday <restart> I went to I went to </> the market

name: emphasis-not-restart
why: “very very good” is emphasis, not a restart. Known gap in the rules.
script: The food was <not restart> very very </> good

name: clean-speech
why: Fluent speech should get no markers at all.
script: I like to walk to work because it is quiet and I can think about the day ahead

name: mixed-monologue
why: A 30-second talk with several kinds of trouble, like a real take. It only gets 2 markers, so the two long pauses should win; the fillers and restart must still be detected.
script: So my hometown is a small city by the sea. In summer the beach is full of families and [2.8 pause] tourists. <fillers maybe> Umm, the best thing about it is, uhh, </> the food, especially the fish market in the morning. <restart maybe> I used to I used to </> go there with my grandfather every Saturday. [1.0 not pause] He knew everyone and he always bought too much. [3.2 pause] I miss that a lot. Now the city is bigger and busier, but the market is still there.

name: pause-other-voice
why: Same freeze in a British male voice, so results do not depend on one voice.
script: The hardest thing about moving was finding a [2.5 pause] good doctor

name: fillers-other-voice
why: Fillers in an Australian voice. (Karen says “uhh” as “ooh”, so both fillers are “umm”.)
script: I think, <fillers> umm, the weather there is, umm, </> much warmer
